body_long:
Lake Como has a new name on its shore. Jumeirah, the Dubai-based luxury group and member of Dubai Holding, is adding Jumeirah Lake Como to its European portfolio. The hotel, formerly Il Sereno Lago di Como, in the village of Torno, will welcome guests from spring 2027. The news was reported on 24 November 2026.

## Forty suites on the water

The redesign is by the architect and designer Patricia Urquiola, who already reworked the suites of Jumeirah Capri Palace. Natural stone and wood, floor-to-ceiling windows and generous terraces set the tone. The hotel is all-suite, with 40 waterfront suites, each with a furnished private terrace.

Two stand out. The Grand Darsena Suite, 200 m², has direct access to the lake for swimming. The Smeraldo Penthouse Suite adds a private garden and a hot tub to its lake views. Guests will also find waterfront restaurants with a refreshed Italian culinary concept, a heated freshwater infinity pool and a Talise Spa planned inside the historic lakeside boathouse. Personal Hosts arrange excursions aboard boats by Cantiere Ernesto Riva.

## A European collection

Thomas B. Meier, chief executive of Jumeirah, presents the project as a way to build on the hotel's architectural character, extending the group's expansion beyond new destinations. Jumeirah Lake Como joins Jumeirah Capri Palace in Italy, alongside Jumeirah Mallorca, Jumeirah Carlton Tower in London and the forthcoming Jumeirah Le Richemond in Geneva.

## The signal

Lake Como has become one of the most competitive luxury destinations in Europe. By taking over a design-led address rather than building, Jumeirah enters the lake with an established hotel and a star designer, and keeps assembling a European collection piece by piece.

Congratulations to the Jumeirah teams on this new address.
summary: The former Il Sereno in Torno becomes Jumeirah Lake Como, an all-suite hotel redesigned by Patricia Urquiola, opening in spring 2027.
title: Jumeirah arrives on Lake Como with the former Il Sereno
why: A Dubai luxury group takes a design icon on Europe's most coveted lake.
